title: Adaptive backpressure & batching for OpenTelemetry exporters (reduce dropped spans under bursty load)
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Goal: Add an adaptive backpressure layer to the OpenTelemetry exporter pipeline used by Redwood tracing hooks so we avoid large numbers of dropped spans during short-term bursty loads while preserving latency SLOs for synchronous requests. This ticket designs and implements a per-tenant adaptive batching + queueing policy with memory guards and fallbacks for Jaeger/Tempo deployments.

Background:
- We currently see dropped spans when collector processes experience sudden traffic spikes or transient backend flakiness (Tempo ingestion throttles, Jaeger backpressure). Existing exporter behavior either blocks request threads (harming latency) or drops spans once the in-memory buffer exceeds a static size.
- Previous work (ENG-9573, ENG-8421) focused on routing and exporter failover; this ticket focuses on the exporter-side buffering and retry/backpressure algorithm.

Design summary (high level):
1) Per-tenant adaptive queue: each tenant/route gets a soft in-memory queue whose size is proportional to their recent sustained throughput and active concurrency. Soft limit reduces to a minimum under low load to conserve memory.
2) Adaptive batch sizing: batch size grows/shrinks based on observed backend ACK latency and error rate. On fast ACKs, batch size increases to improve throughput; on elevated errors/timeouts, batch size decreases immediately.
3) Backpressure signals: when a tenant queue hits its soft limit, the exporter will apply a non-blocking pushback score to the incoming request context (set header/metric that upstream runtime can use to deprioritize non-critical traces). For internal synchronous RPCs where latency is critical, we fall back to sampling reduction rather than blocking.
4) Persistent fallback queue: if memory pressure is sustained and the backend remains unreachable for >30s for a tenant, optionally spill oldest batches to a local rotating file queue (config flag enabled per deployment/private customer). This avoids permanent loss during multi-minute backend outages and is size-capped.
5) Retry policy with jittered exponential backoff and per-batch idempotency markers where supported by downstream (Tempo / Jaeger HTTP).

Telemetry & dashboards to add/change:
- New metrics (per-tenant tags): exporter.queue_length, exporter.batch_size_observed, exporter.dropped_spans_count, exporter.spill_to_disk_count, exporter.retry_count, exporter.backend_5xx_rate, exporter.backend_p99_ack_latency.
- Traces: add internal spans for exporter.enqueue -> exporter.flush -> backend.response to correlate client latency with exporter activity.
- Dashboards: update latency/error dashboards to include exporter.queue_length and spill_to_disk trends and an alert burn rate when dropped_spans_count rises above threshold for customer-impacting services.

Acceptance criteria:
- Under synthetic burst test (10x baseline QPS for 60s), end-to-end client p50 latency must not increase >10% for synchronous calls that have high priority, while total observed dropped spans must be <1% for high-priority tenants and <5% for default tenants.
- Persistent queueing triggers only when backend outage >30s and respects configured disk caps.
- New metrics available in CloudMetrics within 2 minutes of deployment and have dashboards/alerts wired.
- Feature flag exists to disable persistent disk spill for Private customers that disallow local persistence.

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Prototype in a sidecar process: implement adaptive soft-queue + batcher with synthetic backend to validate algorithm. (Engineers: Rohit + Maya)
B) Integrate into main collector/exporter path: add per-tenant queue management, metrics, and unit tests. Add configuration knobs in runtime config (max-queue-per-tenant, spill-to-disk-enabled, min-batch, max-batch).
C) Add persistent rotating file queue implementation (optional behind flag). Ensure encryption-at-rest for Private deployments and KMS hooks for keys.
D) End-to-end tests and load tests: use canary harness in us-west-2; run chaos scenario where Tempo returns 502 for 90s. Verify spill, retries, and eventual drain.
E) Rollout: feature-flagged canary -> 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% across regions with monitoring gates.

Tradeoffs & open decisions:
- In-memory vs persistent: in-memory keeps latency lowest but risks more drops; persistent queue reduces loss but introduces non-trivial operational complexity and must be opt-in for enterprise with compliance constraints. Decision: persistent fallback behind opt-in flag; default disabled for hosted customers.
- Blocking callers vs dropping spans: blocking preserves data but can violate latency SLOs. We will prefer sampling reduction + non-blocking pushback for low priority traces and only block for explicitly annotated high-priority traces (synthetic/diagnostic spans).
- Per-tenant sizing heuristic: initial heuristic based on 95th percentile historic throughput and concurrency; we will refine with production telemetry.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for batch size adaptation logic, queue gateway, and retry/backoff.
- Integration tests that spin up a fake Tempo/Jaeger endpoint that intentionally delays or errors.
- Load tests: see test matrix in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Exporter+Adaptive+Backpressure+Tests (placeholder).
- Security review for persistent spill (ensure encryption + secure deletion).

Docs & rollout notes:
- Confluence design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Adaptive+Exporter+Backpressure (placeholder).
- Ops runbook: how to disable persistent spill, increase per-tenant limits, and manual drain steps.
- Changelog/SDK notes for customers if their sampled trace volumes might be affected by sampling fallback.

Related PRs & artifacts:

- Integration PR (WIP): github.com/redwood/collector/pull/1289 
- Load test harness: github.com/redwood/observability-loadtests/tree/exp/exporter-backpressure
